findings.title: Automatic confirmation does not rearm failed or revoked admission scopes
Late verification cannot overwrite concurrent revocation under the current record CAS
Unscoped legacy drafts are isolated from cross-workspace save, rebind, and delete
Handoff grouping preserves distinct target activations and unknown receivers
Provider-reported cost is shown separately from tokens and any verified bill
Native Escape is delivered to the focused PTY without closing the terminal view
The fixed outer wrapper permits the native read path while denying source, authority, and credential writes
Chronological native Q/A is retained beside managed history without promoting failed or mismatched protocol to success

limitations: User personal UX acceptance remains pending; Codex-operated Chromium and native sessions are technical evidence, not user approval.

The candidate is a read-only frozen export without .git. Independent reconstruction still matches the supplied 194-file candidate SHA-256 and Git tree. The bounded round-three hash check matched all 82 round-three evidence entries, and the preserved prior manifest contains the original 75 entries.

The reviewer-requested normal-host execution of the exact three-test outer-isolation command passed all 3 tests with exit 0 and source unchanged, closing the R2 enforcement-evidence gap. That dynamic command was executed by a fixed external normal-host observer controlled by Codex desktop, not by this Claude session; the prior nested-user-namespace failure remains unchanged in the raw R2 scratch record and is not represented as a new successful Claude execution.

Native evidence proves recorded requested/reported identities, UUID/cwd bindings, terminal behavior, and the actual read-tool result where supplied; physical backend and effective effort remain unknown. Provider-reported cost remains distinct from a verified bill.

The source audit made no model calls, did not read credentials, native transcripts, or hidden reasoning, and made no source, authority, commit, push, merge, Stable-promotion, or user-acceptance changes. Original R1/R2 reports and the old Gate result remain unchanged.
